a.text: I hear leaves blooping and bubbling away inside a scalding hot pot. I love that sound.

There's the static from Dad's radio too, and the oldie hawking on about sharpening your blades, and the sound of the ute's power plant as it drives... I love all that too. But I'm not gonna hear them anymore. Or, well... I won't soon enough.
Here's the fire, burning. Telling me, hey, chin up, just chin up a bit... you know, Dad's hoping you will.
Actually, I think the fire's a little weak. I'll give it a bit of air. Puffff—
Eh? What's that sound I hear...?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Lanns! Can you not dink on your bowl?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: I told you to stop doing that! What if you get on someone's nerves?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: I'll dink on anything I please. Can't I be the boss of my own ute? Besides, with how loud the truck stop is, nobody's gonna be pointing fingers at me!

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Don't make excuses.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: I'm just bored, mate...

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: You're making an awful lot of food today. What's the occasion anyway? I've been waiting ages, I'm starved!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: I had to make some noise to get a message across to the food: 'Don't get cold now, we need to wait for Potlid to join us for our meal.'

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Excuses again... You don't worry about anything, you're like a kid.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: If you're that bored, come help me out in the kitchen!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Oh, but you're the six-star chef here. You're killing it in there, Potlid!

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Would you stop calling me Potlid alrea—

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: —What's this red dish here?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Oh, that's the tomato braised cystybeast!

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: It's fresh from the pot. It'll blow you away!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Tomato braised cystybeast? What's with the color? Shouldn't the broth be a little more yellowy—?
Before she can finish her sentence, Alanna has already rammed her spoon into the piping-hot bowl and scooped an entire slab of cystybeast meat into her mouth.
The food burns her tongue, but Alanna gives the Potlid a thumbs-up nonetheless.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: ...Hm... Mmhmm...

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: It's perfect! That's our truck's six-star chef!

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Hehe~

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: But the meat you brought back this time's especially fresh. I didn't have to use a lot of seasoning to make it taste good!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Really? Looks like the market man gave us the freshest on hand, knowing we're leaving. Guess it was worth buying from him for two years.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Don't say things like that, Lanns. I think he's been real good to us from the very beginning, going by what you've told me.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: I'm picturing a kinda short, good-tempered man in a dirty apron. A short, fat, middle-aged man.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Yeah, nah, that's not what he looks like. When he stands in front of his shop holding a cleaver, not a single person dares to swipe even a single carrot from the market.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Haha. When you get older, I'll let you walk around town yourself.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: That reminds me. When was the last time we had tomato braised cysty?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: The last time...?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: It was probably when we first ate together.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: And you made that meal yourself!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Oh, that does feel like a long time ago. You still remember?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Of course!

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: You said 'cooking's just one of the things I'm good at,' but then you made an in-sane-ly sour tomato braised cystybeast.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: *cough*, how was I supposed to know those tomatoes were gonna be that sour? The broth was bright and yellow. It looked so tasty.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: I still remember the look on your face after you gave it a taste.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Wh-What does it matter if it helps fill our tummies? Flavor comes second! And didn't you finish all of yours?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: It's not good to waste food! Besides...

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Ah, let's not talk about the past. I don't want the food to get cold because you can't stop complaining.
Potlid lightly touches the bowl, and suddenly the braised meat becomes just as piping hot as when it was fresh out of the pot.
Amid the rising white steam, Alanna's expression grows stern.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Hey!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Didn't we agree not to use Arts for little things like that?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: But this is the fastest way to warm it up...

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: I'm just heating the food up. Just a quick use. It's nothing to worry about!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Whatever. It's your health, not mine.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: But as soon as we get to Iron Carrot City, we need to find you a teacher who can teach you real proper casting.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Come on, tuck in. What are you waiting for?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Let me enjoy the view first.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: You always look so happy when you eat. It puts a smile on my face just watching you.
Potlid takes a cloth and wipes clean the broth that's spilled over the bowl, then wipes her hands.
She takes a few thick books from the shelf and stacks them on her seat, one-by-one, before sitting on top of them.
Potlid places one arm on the table flat while her other hand props her head up, and she looks at Alanna with a smile on her face.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: We're going to have to return the truck when we get to Iron Carrot City, and they'll shut the route down forever.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Yeah.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Think you'll miss it?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: ...Not really.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Warmy never gets sad.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Well, alright then.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: In that case, after this route's suspended, do you still wanna stay on my truck?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: After we return it to the company, they'll probably keep it around. Though I doubt it'll go to the stops we took before.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Even so, I won't let it get to me... Yeah, nuh-uh, I won't!

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: As long as you're right here by my side, there's nothing to be unhappy about!
Alanna reaches out to pat Potlid on the head. Her ears twitch in response.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Hehehe...

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: What's wrong?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Th-That kinda tickles...
Seeing the young Cautus's reaction, Alanna laughs.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Then—

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Then, my wonderful, perpetually-smiley Potlid. Help me run some errands later, will ya?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Huh? But it's been so long since I've gone into town...

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: You'll be fine.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: See, I took the safety valve off to make it go faster, and I can't have the company finding that out when they inspect the ute.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: So we need a new safety valve right quick.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: And we'll also need some daily necessities for a long trip. The workers said they'd bring us some, but I said no.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Hm... the guys at the motor pool know you're leaving?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Yeah, but I still have heaps of things that I need to deal with here. If I were to go, I might not be done by tomorrow morning.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Do they know you're taking me with you?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Hm, I suppose.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Anyhow, that's why I'm counting on you to take care of that. You're a young lady already anyway.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: And here—
Alanna passes Potlid a paper scrap with some wobbly writing on it.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Sell those things out the front door. We should be able to get some money out of them.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: As for the rest, follow the shopping list. Here's my purse. Take it with you.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: I still have one last bit of work to handle.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: So this is the last...

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Let's divvy up the work and get this done. Divide and conquer.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Okay... let's do it!

steps.name: General Storekeeper
steps.text: ...Then the metal crab woke up. It got to its feet, snipped twice, and carved the tower crane into pieces.

steps.name: General Storekeeper
steps.text: Everyone took a good look, and turns out all that reinforced concrete didn't make a dent in its shell when everything came crumbling down. Of course they dropped their shovels and blowtorches and ran for their lives.

steps.name: General Storekeeper
steps.text: Haha, how's that? I heard it's based on a real story, real people, uh, crab and all. This is what we're showing for tonight's open-air movie night, over at the slag heap.

steps.name: General Storekeeper
steps.text: Eh, no need to thank me. I've never seen you around, so you have to be new here.

steps.name: General Storekeeper
steps.text: Let me go more into the rules of our ball and card games here. Each factory district has different rules. You know that, right?

steps.name: Reticent Customer
steps.text: ...I just want a sandbeast.

steps.name: General Storekeeper
steps.text: Ahem... Fine.

steps.name: General Storekeeper
steps.text: I have a few of them in this basket here. Pick whichever you want. All my sandbeasts are well-trained. They eat and sleep and follow their masters close.

steps.name: General Storekeeper
steps.text: You really don't wanna talk about anything else? Like, fine weather today, isn't it? It's not often we get a day without a sandstorm out here. Makes work much easier—

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: W-Watch out! Out of the way. Out of the way—

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: I-I can't stoppppppp—!

steps.name: General Storekeeper
steps.text: Crikey, who's having such a little kid cart all these things? Don't they know this street goes downslope...?

steps.name: General Storekeeper
steps.text: ...Little girl, you with me? You think you got brain damage?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: *sobs*...

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: I'm okay! I'm not a baby anymore! I'll be fine!

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Ah! It took me so much work to pile up the pots and dishes. Now they're all over the ground...
The little girl prepares to bend down to pick up a big pot. At the same time, a hand reaches out for it.
The two both take a reflexive step back; Potlid nervously tugs her own sleeve.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Um... Miss, I can pick these things up myself. You don't have to help me.

steps.name: Reticent Customer
steps.text: Okay.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Also, thanks for stopping my hand truck there!

steps.name: Reticent Customer
steps.text: Yeah, you didn't say you wanted to stop, but there's a recycling facility up ahead. It wouldn't be good if you crashed into it.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Huh...? Okay, you have a point!

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: I'm sorry, Mister. My things are blocking your shop's entrance. I'll clean it all up right away!

steps.name: General Storekeeper
steps.text: It's fine, little girl. Take your time.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Oh, hold on, so this is the 'Tinny Longears' general store.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Mister, I'm here to talk business!

steps.name: General Storekeeper
steps.text: Business? Hahaha... shouldn't someone be watching you?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: I don't need her to help me with this. She has her own work to do. We're dividing and conquering.

steps.name: General Storekeeper
steps.text: Mhm... Alright. Wait here for a sec.

steps.name: General Storekeeper
steps.text: Girl, you picked out a sandbeast yet?

steps.name: Reticent Customer
steps.text: Let me have another look.

steps.name: General Storekeeper
steps.text: I'll deal with the little girl first, then. C'mon, what are you buying?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: First things first. I need to sell some things before I buy anything.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Take a look at these pots and pans, as well as this Originium gas cooker. I'm selling them all. I heard that second-hand kitchenware that's kept well and clean sells for a lot of money.

steps.name: General Storekeeper
steps.text: *cough*, *cough*... A pot so scorched, even its handle's black, a fork with broken teeth, and scrap sheet metal... You're trying to sell this?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: With the money I make from selling these and the change in my purse, I know I'll have enough for a safety valve, an electrode holder, spray paint...

steps.name: General Storekeeper
steps.text: *sigh*, how about this? Bring everything you want to buy to the counter. I'll give you a discount and take your wares based on the total price. Whatever's left over, I won't take.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Nuh-uh, I have to sell all these things.

steps.name: General Storekeeper
steps.text: I can treat you to a cold carrot.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Okay!

steps.name: General Storekeeper
steps.text: It's a deal, then. Let's see. This gas cooker is more than enough. Take the rest of that garbage back with you, okay?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: On second thought... nuh-uh.

steps.name: General Storekeeper
steps.text: You're a weird one, little girl... Why are you insisting on selling all those things? If you didn't look like such a nice little bun, I'd be thinking you committed some kind of crime and came here to get rid of evidence.

steps.name: General Storekeeper
steps.text: And let's be real. I don't know you from Bruce. How am I supposed to just offload the garbage you hauled here? What if you turn out to be an Infected?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: I knew it! An afternoon wasn't going to be enough to sell all of it! Nuh-uh, I told her, and she didn't believe me.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Alright, I'll have to report back, then think of something!

steps.name: General Storekeeper
steps.text: Hold on, little one. Who sent you?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Huh? Lanns. Alanna of the Barrenlands.

steps.name: General Storekeeper
steps.text: Alright, alright. I don't know you, but I do know her. Look at her dumping her work on a little girl like you. Not that I'm surprised.

steps.name: General Storekeeper
steps.text: Here, a footstool. That way you can get a better view while I tally the numbers up. Tell her I'll take her things for now, and whenever she gets a day off, she owes me a meal.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Huh? Why the change of heart...?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Hm, I guess it's fair. I'm not a kid anymore. If I'm asked to do something, I get it done.

steps.name: General Storekeeper
steps.text: What's the matter? You're weren't happy when I wouldn't 'talk business,' and you're also unhappy that I'm taking these off your hands?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Huh? Yeah, nah. I've been happy the whole time.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Hmm... the safety valve model that Lanns told me to get's not on the shelf.

steps.name: General Storekeeper
steps.text: Let's see...

steps.name: General Storekeeper
steps.text: Didn't this model go obsolete ages ago? Ever since the union set the regs, the guidebook's been full of tips to never buy that junk again.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Nuh-uh, I have to go look for it elsewhere. I'll find it! Mister, look after the hand truck for me!

steps.name: General Storekeeper
steps.text: *sigh*... I really need to talk to Alanna about this.

steps.name: General Storekeeper
steps.text: What about you, Miss? Have you picked one yet? Or do you have something else in mind?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Agh, what do I even do with you? Gimme the spanner. I'll do it. I know my ute better than anybody else.

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: Hey, you hired me for this, Alanna. You want to save yourself some money, come out and say it.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: I'm not always tight on money like your broke arse. I'm no alcoholic, and I don't drive my truck so bad that it breaks down every other day.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Besides, if I do less work than you, how am I supposed to boast to Potlid about my skills?

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: Hahaha, that little runt...?

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: This thing we're taking apart right now. That's where she sleeps, right?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Uh-huh.

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: Hahahaha, really?! Alright, I'll give it to you. I lost this time.

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: We all thought you were just talking big.

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: Given your temper, shouldn't you have made her somebody else's problem a long time ago?

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: —Uh, my bad. Stop glaring.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: My temper? Hmph, who do you even think I am? I took her in because all of you bet against me having the patience to take care of a kid, and I wasn't going to take that slander lying down.

spans.text: Hmph, who do you even think I am? I took her in because all of you bet against me having the patience to take care of a kid, and I wasn't going to take that slander lying down.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Look down on me again, and the next time I'm back, I'll kick a ball into your faces.

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: Eh, it's mainly that we haven't seen her the last two years. We only have your word to go on.

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: You got your treads chewed by a big beckbeast, you swapped the control valve at the last minute under Catastrophe clouds to speed up your transport, you caught a passenger that got blasted into the sky by a geyser... Everything you say is like it's all happened.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: That all actually happened, I'm telling you.

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: Fine, it happened. Now why did you keep her locked away in the truck the whole time, never letting her out to spend time with the rest of us?

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: —Surely she didn't want to stay shut up in there?

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: ...If that's really the case, what are you planning to do tomorrow when the truck's out of commission?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: ...I'll figure something out once I get to Carrot's. The company has to give me a new route, right?

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: You'll figure something out... Hold on, you're going to Iron Carrot City to wait for a new route instead of staying here?

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: You're never coming back?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Hm, this is the only one I could get... It's not quite what Lanns told me to find, but the shop said we should at least be able to plug it in. It'll be fine.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: It's getting dark. If I don't hurry and get back, we won't finish everything we have to do.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Lanns... should be back too by now?

steps.name: Jittery Passenger
steps.text: Uh, little girl, hello? You're walking kinda leisurely, not like you're trying to catch a ride...

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Huh? Do I look leisurely? Hehe...

steps.name: Jittery Passenger
steps.text: If I might have a little of your time, would you happen to know when the last transport to Iron Carrot City leaves?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Half past nine at night.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: I know that route better than anybody.

steps.name: Jittery Passenger
steps.text: Oh, okay. Appreciate it, kid.

steps.name: Jittery Passenger
steps.text: Half past nine... I still have some time.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: *sigh*, I'm really worried about Lanns for some reason. What's going on...?
There is an old, abandoned workshop belonging to the vehicle located at the city transport gateway. Its lights, familiar as ever, can be seen through its windows.
Potlid wipes the dust off the window and peeks inside—
The passage leading to the exit bears the 'workplace fatigue' from the workers' frantic movement, all the loading and unloading they perform every day.
They say the passage is old and smoothed out, just like the bottom of the tin lunch box that the old factory director has used and washed for two decades.
As the workers cheer on, a metal ball, or more precisely, an amalgamation of a variety of scrap metals compressed together and polished into a ball, is dropped onto the smooth surface.
The ball rolls forward.

steps.name: Worker 'Brake'
steps.text: Good shot, mate!

steps.name: Worker 'Motor'
steps.text: Beautiful, and you knocked them all down in one go... Good one, Alanna!

steps.name: Worker 'Brake'
steps.text: Let's see. Eighteen, nineteen... You're ahead by twenty. How are we supposed to catch up?

steps.name: Worker 'Brake'
steps.text: Charlie, you sproglet. Let's call it quits while our score doesn't look too terrible. Don't embarrass the factory!

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: Alright, alright. Just shut up and watch. Let me show you wankers what a perfect shot looks like.

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: Instead of worrying about me, maybe start racking your brains to figure out how we'll decorate tonight's send-off party for Alanna...

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: First, we'll make it a welcome party. We'll welcome Alanna as a proper member of the Rustdreg Town motor pool family.

steps.name: Worker 'Motor'
steps.text: Really now? If you don't knock all the pins down in this one go, you aren't getting another shot at it.

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: Put a sock in it.
He bends down to put the fallen pins upright, and rubs his hands against his trouser pockets, his sweat leaving a clearly visible mark on the fabric.
He picks up the ball, places his toes just slightly before the foul line, and stares straight ahead—

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Hold on.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Charlie, that's enough.

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: I'm in the lead for now, and you still have a chance to overtake me. We could put our argument on hold—Considering the score, it should be an acceptable outcome for both of us.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Let's call it a draw. What do you say?

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: Alanna, forget this place. There's not a single person in all the matches ever played in the RMIA who ever tried to pull a trick like this.

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: If I'm remembering right, we agreed that if I win, you stay. If you win, we won't keep you, and you can go wherever.

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: And now you're asking for a draw...? What do you want us to do? Cut you in half and have one half drive your truck, while the other half stays here?

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: Or are you going to spend half of your time on your new life and the other half with your old friends?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: I'll pass. I'm not like those new factory district reps.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: They announce their newest expansion plans at their morning conferences, supervise mine work in the afternoons, and go to some boring social engagements in the evenings.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: I've got more than enough on my plate, and I can't be in two places at once. I only have enough sanity in me to hold the gear lever, at most leaning one ear closer to the passengers to eavesdrop on their funny stories.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: So, here's my suggestion—

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: I'll head to Carrot's to get everything dealt with. The next time I'm back, I'll talk to all of you about joining the motor pool.

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: So you're saying you're never coming back!

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: Why? Because of our bet? Because of that little kid?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Lanns?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: ...Potlid?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Wh-Wh-Why are you bowling here? Didn't you... Didn't you say you had lots to take care of?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Uh, we haven't settled our bet, so of course I have to take care of this—

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: (Sighs)

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: (Whispers) Lanns... you lazy cystybeast.
Potlid raises her hand up high and shoves Alanna's shoulder as hard as she can.
Her sleeve slides down to reveal a black, irregularly-shaped crystal cluster. Not even the bracelet that Alanna gave her is able to hide its luster.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Hm? Why are your friends all looking at me?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: —Ugh, they're just curious. Come, we're going back to the ute.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Woah...

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: What do you think? I'm willing to bet no one could tell that just four hours ago, there used to be an illegal kitchen here, right?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: That's what you get with the best vehicle makeover hands in the entire district. It's not every day I get to put my skills to work.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Yep, I really can't tell at all...

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: But Lanns... You didn't tell me you were taking it apart...

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: ...Even so, it's amazing!

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: You told me the work we had left was a huge pain, and you might not finish if you had to do it all alone. Isn't that why you asked me to buy all those things?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: But not only are you all done, you're bowling with the men here. You're even having a lolly water and reading magazines!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Uh, haha, but of course.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Anyhow, we only have three minor problems left now.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: First off, we need to use spraypaint to cover up the smoke damaged wall here. Let me show you how it works first. After that, you have fun with the other two cans.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: I think I might've started a few too many fires...

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Next, we have the power plant pipeline's safety valve.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Oh, I couldn't find the kind you wanted. Does that mean...?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Does that mean we won't be able to hand in the truck tomorrow?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Don't worry. I knew you wouldn't be able to find a model that old.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Ehh...?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: You see, we're getting our truck inspected and upgraded because even though all the other parts are fairly new, the power plant is too old.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: No one cared about it before, but the unions in Big Pillar have been clamoring for standardization.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Hah, 'standardization.' Sounds like a pretty cool word, right? You can think of it as setting up rules.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: The old power plant's problems don't bother me, but the union says they're switching over to the top-of-the-line thingies in the ads for our own good, and I think they have a point.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Anyway, it's because ours is against the rules that we're going to get a new one from a transport company in Carrot's tomorrow. We'll be fine, even if this valve isn't a perfect fit.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: We just have one last run. As long as it gets our ute to its final destination, it's more than enough.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: And if we end up having to use the backup pipeline, then... I'll need you to help me out.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Just like before, I'll ask you to go down to the power plant to take a look at things, and you'll need to report anything that seems off right away.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Mm... Okay!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Finally...

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: This is the 'Decommissioning Report' we need to hand over to the station when we leave. Once we're gone, we aren't coming back.
Alanna stops for a bit and glances at Potlid.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Hah, all these silly formalities, right? And they barely gave me any heads up. I asked Thick Palm Parker to teach me how to fill out the form, and it took two whole hours. I didn't have time to take it to the station today.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: You did pretty good today, so I'll turn in this report tomorrow morning on my own. You can stay in the toolroom and sleep in!

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: If you're sad, it's okay to let it out...

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: ...If we get a route change, you probably won't get a lot of chances to see your mates here, right?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: That's why I'll hand in the report tomorrow!

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: That way, you can spend a bit more time with your mates, and you won't be so sad over not seeing them anymore!

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: My kitchen's gone now, but when we get to our new home, once our house is built, I'll make the sweet meat soup that always put a smile on your face.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Haha, sounds good.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Ugh! You slapped my back too hard!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: You're growing up, aren't you? You'll get used to it.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Okay, now catch.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Tonight, I'll let you have lolly waters with me and go to bed an hour later than before.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: *yawn*—So tired.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: But I won't get lost! I'm not a little kid. I can read a map!

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Yep, take a turn here, go upstairs right ahead...

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Huh...? The man from yesterday is still there. Did he miss his ride?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Not only is he sitting in the same place, he's in the same pose, and looks just as depressed. Wow, incredible...

steps.name: Jittery Passenger
steps.text: Oh, it's you, little girl... G-Good morning... Perfect timing.

steps.name: Jittery Passenger
steps.text: Uh, when's the earliest truck to Iron Carrot City today?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: I'm actually that truck's—

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: No, I mean... I'm taking that truck, too!

steps.name: Jittery Passenger
steps.text: Looks like I'll make it...

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: I can take you there. That way, you won't miss it!

steps.name: Jittery Passenger
steps.text: N-N-No thanks!

steps.name: Jittery Passenger
steps.text: Sorry, I... I really appreciate it, but... uh, I want to sit here a little longer.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Are you... waiting for someone?

steps.name: Jittery Passenger
steps.text: Me? No, I... Uh, what makes you think that?

steps.name: Familiar Kind Man
steps.text: Come, Warmy. No more waiting. Let's go back into the hut tonight.

steps.name: Familiar Kind Man
steps.text: These things happen.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Because...

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: It's a very normal thing to wait for someone.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Okay, I'll be on my way. Bye bye! I hope you'll get to see the person you're waiting for!

steps.name: Jittery Passenger
steps.text: No, um, I'm scared to death... I don't want to see...

steps.name: Jittery Passenger
steps.text: ...*sigh*, Cautus kids sure run quick... I should, uh, thank her nonetheless.

steps.name: Office PA
steps.text: Next. Bring your documents into the office.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: (Stands on tiptoes) How far away is the office? I can't see it at all from the line...

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: What should I do? It's almost time to leave. I don't think I'll get it handed in time.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: So many people here this early. Maybe luck's not on my side. Even a big girl can't help it when she's unlucky.

steps.name: No-Nonsense Woman
steps.text: *Sigh*, yeah, there are too many people here. Nothing wrong with the union trying to make the event seem more above-board, but they didn't have to handle both beauty pageant registrations and government forms in the exact same place, did they?

steps.name: No-Nonsense Woman
steps.text: This is almost exactly how everybody used to line up in front of Grandma's room to complain!

steps.name: No-Nonsense Woman
steps.text: Good thing I'm taking care of this. If it'd been the Doctor or Amiya here, it would've been a huge headache, what with how much work they have on their hands.

steps.name: No-Nonsense Woman
steps.text: *sigh*, Amiya, Amiya... She's just a teenager. Why exactly does she have so much on her shoulders...?

steps.name: No-Nonsense Woman
steps.text: Right, little girl, you said you were in a rush? Small and waifish as you are, you wouldn't be here for the beauty pageant, right?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Huh? N-No, I'm here to hand in our 'Decommissioning Report.' Here, it's this one!

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: If we don't hand it in today, then it won't get decommissioned, right...?

steps.name: No-Nonsense Woman
steps.text: Oh, now that's easy. Just let me take care of it.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Huh—?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: But it's our truck that's getting decommissioned... Do you know Lanns?

steps.name: No-Nonsense Woman
steps.text: Yeah, nah.

steps.name: No-Nonsense Woman
steps.text: But you couldn't be the driver, could you?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Um, no...

steps.name: No-Nonsense Woman
steps.text: Yep, yep. That's what I am talking about. The report just needs to be handed in. Doesn't matter who does the handing.

steps.name: No-Nonsense Woman
steps.text: I need to line up here anyway. Taking your report to the office desk there is nothing. Just leave it to me, and get back to your ride!

steps.name: No-Nonsense Woman
steps.text: Oh... why so glum? Is there still something worrying you?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Huh? Do I look...? No, I can't be like this.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Um... Here, the report.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Thanks, Miss. You're too kind!

steps.name: No-Nonsense Woman
steps.text: (This girl's condition...)

steps.name: No-Nonsense Woman
steps.text: Here, kid. This is for you.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Um... it's a card?

steps.name: No-Nonsense Woman
steps.text: A business card. Remember to give it to your family. Might come in handy one day.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Hurry up! The passengers will be here any minute!

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: *pant*, *pant*... Coming!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: You're gonna have to hide in the toolroom this trip.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: I'll be fine. Remember, I stayed in there for a long time in the beginning!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Also, you can still use the little terminal here to check the monitoring screens. You can see every person on the truck... Guess I didn't have to say, huh?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Yeah.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Alright, I'm off to the driver's cabin.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: I finished so much in such a short amount of time.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Even though I ran into lots of trouble, and even though Lanns said there probably wasn't enough time... we still managed to get the ute into shape to hand back, and we took care of all the paperwork.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Oh, the man from the station finally made it in. Thank goodness... Right, I even helped someone with the schedule.

steps.name: All-Transport-Trucks Broadcast
steps.text: The transport vehicle's entrance is now closed. The vehicle will soon be powered on. Please take your seats or find a suitable area to affix your folding chair, bench, or mat...

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: ...I did such a great job, I should be happy, even proud of myself!

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: But, but...

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Actually...

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: I don't care what happens, I wish our truck didn't have to be retired—!

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: I... I still haven't got to see...

steps.name: All-Transport-Trucks Broadcast
steps.text: This vehicle's being hijacked. We're heading to the Grinning Valley.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: ...Huh?
Potlid looks at the display panel where the driver cabin's monitoring screen is shown.
The unfamiliar voice heard through the broadcast belongs to the strange woman she met yesterday. She's holding Alanna's broadcast mic with one hand.
Her other hand is steadily holding her crossbow, with its bolt pressed against the side of Alanna's neck.
She stares at Potlid with a cold glare through the monitoring camera's lens, perhaps noticing the subtle movement of its shift in angle.

steps.name: All-Transport-Trucks Broadcast
steps.text: Anyone not heading to the Grinning Valley can get off now, driver included.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Huh...? It's a real truckjacking?
